title: Generic Enums
snippet: Enums with type parameters like Maybe<T>
description: Generic enums use type parameters to create reusable algebraic data types. A classic example is a Maybe<T> type which represents an optional value - either Some(T) containing a value or None. Generic enums enable type-safe error handling, optional values, and generic containers. When constructing or matching generic enums, you must specify type arguments (e.g., Maybe<int>). The compiler performs monomorphization, generating specialized code for each concrete type used. This example demonstrates a custom Maybe<T> with explicit type parameters in construction and pattern matching. Note: BPL's standard library provides Option<T> - we use Maybe here to demonstrate creating your own generic enum.
